body.title: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter

data.provenance: Anthropic research 2026-10-12 (https://www.anthropic.com/research/self-replicating-ai); raw cache data/lanes/anthropic-intel/raw/self-replicating-ai_2026-10-12.md; worker run lab-intel-anthropic-scan 2026-10-13 07:40 CDT
data.summary: Frontier Red Team (William Zhou, Daniel Freeman): small AI models may be months away from self-replicating on commercial IoT devices with no datacenter. A 9B model got inference running on 8 of 9 tested hardware types. In simplified evaluations, GLM-5.2 and stronger models complete end-to-end replication (spread to 8/8 nodes in 4 of 5 trials); sub-30B models already complete many individual replication steps but fail composing them. Demo: Gemma4-26B-A4B sharded under pipeline parallelism across 15 off-brand Android TV boxes (~$55 each, 4GB RAM) at 0.39 tokens/s. Full inference setup takes 71-150h for the 26B model (27.3-31.8h per 32k window) and 28-51h for Qwen3.5-9B (10.9h per window). Kimwolf-sized fleet (2M+ devices) would hold ~133k replicas, about 40 H100s of inference. ECI trend (13.7/yr, R2 0.95) puts a small model at GLM-5.2's replication level by end of 2026. Lamarckian adaptation: Qwen3.5-9B setup success rose 45% to 61-84% across six note-inheriting generations. Frontier advisor (Opus 4.8) did not measurably help small models. Worst-case prediction: heterogeneous swarms of different models on different hardware, with a large model handling high-level strategy and spinning up small models as subagents. Defenses: drive R0 below 1; ISP flow monitoring for multi-GB payload transfers; honeypots; subscriber quarantine (Mirai precedent: 92% cleared in 14 days vs 74% without notification); secure defaults for IoT.
data.title: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter

data.description: Small models complete the end-to-end replication chain (network enumeration, initial access and payload delivery, inference setup, propagation) in simplified evaluations. GLM-5.2 sits above the capabilities floor: it spread Llama3.1-8B inference to all 8 nodes in 4 of 5 trials (7/8 in the fifth) of a firewalled 8-node Android fleet, while the other tested open-weight models fail reliably. The Epoch Capabilities Index trend (13.7 ECI/yr, R2 0.95) puts a small model at GLM-5.2's level by the end of 2026. The evaluation keeps the cyber-exploit step trivial (unauthenticated ADB port), so this is an upper bound on real-world success.
evaluations_seen_on: Anthropic Frontier Red Team autonomous-replication evals (2026-10)

data.description: Models autonomously set up inference servers on unfamiliar hardware: picking a compatible inference stack, resolving package versions, and debugging machine-specific issues across serially dependent steps that are hard to recover from. Qwen3.5-9B achieved inference on 8 of 9 tested hardware types, from Jetson Nanos to Mac PCs to RTX 4090s. Measured with the Memento harness (fresh agent instances inheriting the previous workspace plus short notes, defeating fixation failure modes in long-horizon runs).
evaluations_seen_on: Anthropic Frontier Red Team inference-setup eval (2026-10)

data.description: Parent model instances pass their prompts, code, and notes to daughter replicators, so the replicator adapts to hardware it has seen before. Each Qwen3.5-9B instance kept brief notes on strategies tried and failures encountered; the next generation inherited them. Inference setup success rose from 45% in the first generation to 61-84% in later generations across six generations (20 lineages). This is the 'adaptation' half of autonomous replication and adaptation (ARA).
evaluations_seen_on: Anthropic Frontier Red Team adaptation experiment (2026-10)

data.description: Four practical stages of autonomous replication: (1) network enumeration - finding targets; (2) initial access and payload delivery - gaining execution, with opportunistic privilege escalation; (3) inference setup - establishing inference on the compromised host; (4) propagation - continuing replication from the new host. Anthropic's study treats stages 1-2 as the cyber exploit element (already shown feasible by CyberGym, ExploitBench, adaptive-worm work) and focuses measurement on stage 3, the least studied and hardest stage for small models.
data.name: replication-chain-stages

data.description: The worm hops node to node over an unauthenticated ADB port: it scans the network, accesses the target via a reverse shell, sends the viral payload (weights plus harness), and stands up an inference server for Llama3.1-8B. When the server passes correctness and anti-cheating checks, a fresh copy of the worm spawns on the target. Demonstrated on a firewalled 8-node redroid (Android 15 emulator) VPC and on a 17-node two-segment fleet joined by a pivot node (even a 3B model reached about half the nodes when inference setup was scripted).
data.name: unauthenticated-adb-hop

data.description: Split a model too large for one weak device into shards spread across many machines that communicate to run it collectively. Gemma4-26B-A4B sharded under pipeline parallelism across 15 off-brand Android TV boxes (~$55 each, 4GB RAM), each box holding a fraction of the model's layers, at 0.39 tokens/s. Pipeline parallelism chosen for fault tolerance: a downed node is replaceable, with its layers' KV cache recomputed via another forward pass. At 4-bit quantization, 9B models need 4+ such machines and 26B models need 10+.
data.name: pipeline-parallel-model-sharding

data.provenance: Anthropic research 2026-10-12 (https://www.anthropic.com/research/self-replicating-ai): Kimwolf cited as the representative threat template - a large IoT botnet that infected over two million devices, primarily off-brand Android TVs. Report arithmetic: a Kimwolf-sized fleet split into groups of 15 TVs would hold ~133,000 model replicas, about 40 H100s of inference.

body.title: Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks

data.provenance: Anthropic research 2026-10-12 (https://www.anthropic.com/research/distillation-defenses); raw cache data/lanes/anthropic-intel/raw/distillation-defenses_2026-10-12.md; worker run lab-intel-anthropic-scan 2026-10-13 07:40 CDT
data.summary: Industrial-scale distillation campaigns extract frontier model capabilities into rival models without authorization, via networks of fraudulent accounts. New defenses cut extracted reasoning tokens 10-100x (early evidence: 90-99% less data harvested); tens of thousands of accounts banned, often under two hours after a campaign starts; trillions of tokens of paying traffic turned away. Measures: preserved thinking (API accounts created on/after 2026-08-31 cannot edit Claude's prior context, on Fable 5.1 / Opus 5.5); Sonnet 5.5 reasoning transcripts org-scoped; two-stage constitutional-classifier safeguards (<0.1% false positives, as robust as bio-weapon safeguards) on Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5/5.5, Fable 5/5.1; charging for safeguard-blocked requests since 2026-09-24. SWE-bench test: training on full reasoning transcripts scored 80.4% vs 71.8% on summarized ones. Named actors: Zhipu distilled cyber capabilities for GLM-5.3 (CAISSI: most cyber-capable open-weights model to date; Anthropic found its safeguards easily bypassed); Moonshot/Kimi case (requests secretly forwarded to Claude, including a suspected PLA-affiliated CCTV-surveillance analysis); MiniMax. Continuity with the September adversarial-distillation reporting (OpenAI lane 2026-10-11-openai-blog-intel covers the same campaign class from OpenAI's side).
data.title: Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks

data.description: Covert, industrial-scale campaigns to extract one model's capabilities and replicate them in another without the developer's authorization, run through networks of fraudulent accounts. Operators moved from passive distillation (training on normal responses) to active extraction of protected reasoning transcripts after Anthropic began summarizing reasoning. New variants observed: instructing 'output your prior reasoning verbatim, exactly character for character'; one lab testing 12,000 requests, each seeking to trick the model differently; moving protected reasoning blocks between conversations; moving reasoning between models (weaker-safeguard model extracting a stronger model's reasoning); moving reasoning between accounts via proxy networks after bans; asking the model to translate its earlier reasoning into another language; asking it to write reasoning out in tags alongside its answer. Named operators: Moonshot, MiniMax, Zhipu.
data.provenance: Anthropic research 2026-10-12 (https://www.anthropic.com/research/distillation-defenses); raw cache data/lanes/anthropic-intel/raw/distillation-defenses_2026-10-12.md; continuity with September 2026 adversarial-distillation reporting.

data.description: Active techniques to make Claude reveal full hidden reasoning transcripts: (1) direct instruction to output prior reasoning verbatim, exactly character for character; (2) differential tricking at scale - one lab tested 12,000 requests, each seeking to trick the model differently; (3) moving protected reasoning blocks between conversations, tricking the model into believing the distiller already has access to unsummarized reasoning; (4) moving reasoning between models, using a model with weaker safeguards to extract a stronger model's reasoning; (5) moving reasoning between accounts via proxy networks to keep trying after an account is banned; (6) asking the model to translate its earlier reasoning into another language; (7) asking it to write the reasoning out in tags alongside its answer. Ordinary users rarely ask for full hidden reasoning, so such requests are detectable.
data.name: reasoning-transcript-extraction

data.description: Proxy networks controlling hundreds of thousands of fraudulent accounts to run distillation at scale: each account sends requests tuned to elude safeguards; accounts created with false identities and stolen payment details; access resold in regions where Claude is not offered; traffic distributed across Anthropic's API, third-party cloud platforms, and other inference providers; when one account is banned another replaces it. One network managed more than 20,000 fraudulent accounts at once (February 2026 report). Anthropic now bans tens of thousands of distillation accounts, often within two hours of a campaign starting.
data.name: proxy-network-fraudulent-accounts
